title: The Evolutionary Origin of Values: implications for AI alignment, sentience and existential risk
abstract: arXiv:2608.03361v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: AI systems based on Large Language Models (LLMs) have prompted fears that they may harbor hidden goals, seek to dominate or eliminate humanity, or even suffer as sentient beings. We address these concerns by tracing the evolutionary origin of value in biological organisms. Values emerge from autopoiesis: living systems must actively maintain themselves against perturbation and dissipation. Natural selection has equipped them with hierarchies of "vicarious selectors" that guide their behavior toward fitness. LLMs, by contrast, are allopoietic and allotelic: they produce outputs for others, and their goals derive from user prompts rather than an autonomous drive. They lack the intrinsic motivation for self-preservation, dominance, or resource competition that underlies existential-risk scenarios, and the embodied vulnerability required for feeling or suffering. translated_title: 价值的进化起源：对人工智能对齐、感知和存在风险的影响
translated_abstract: 基于大型语言模型（LLMs）的人工智能系统引发了人们的担忧，即它们可能隐藏着不可告人的目标，寻求主导或消灭人类，甚至可能作为有感知的生物而遭受痛苦。我们通过追溯生物有机体中价值的进化起源来解决这些问题。价值源于自创生：生命系统必须主动维持自身免受扰动和耗散。自然选择为它们配备了分层的“替代选择器”，引导其行为趋向适应性。相比之下，LLMs是异源性和异目的性的：它们为他人产生输出，其目标源自用户提示而非自主驱动力。它们缺乏自我保存、主导或资源竞争的内在动机，而这些动机正是存在风险情景的基础，也缺乏感受或痛苦所需的具身脆弱性。尽管如此，由于LLMs从人类生成的数据中学习统计模式，
tldr: 本文通过追溯价值的进化起源，论证了LLMs缺乏自我保存和感知的内在驱动力，从而降低了存在风险，但需关注其从人类数据中学习的统计模式。
en_tdlr: This paper traces the evolutionary origin of values to argue that LLMs lack intrinsic drives for self-preservation and sentience, mitigating existential risks, while noting their reliance on statistical patterns from human data.
